answer: A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The lantern multiplier is published, charged in velvet, and wharf lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 12 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 875 identities would post 1377 proofs and burn roughly 43 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
